name: open-remote-ssh
description: Use any remote machine with a SSH server as your development environment.

remote.SSH.path.description: The absolute file path to the SSH executable. When set, this SSH binary will be used for connections instead of the default 'ssh' command.

remote.SSH.configFile.description: The absolute file path to a custom SSH config file.

remote.SSH.connectTimeout.description: Specifies the timeout in seconds used for the SSH command that connects to the remote.

remote.SSH.defaultExtensions.description: List of extensions that should be installed automatically on all SSH hosts.

remote.SSH.enableDynamicForwarding.description: Whether to use SSH dynamic forwarding to allow setting up new port tunnels over an existing SSH connection.

remote.SSH.enableAgentForwarding.markdownDescription: Enable fixing the remote environment so that the SSH config option `ForwardAgent` will take effect as expected from VS Code's remote extension host.

remote.SSH.remotePlatform.description: A map of the remote hostname to the platform for that remote. Valid values: linux, macos, windows.

remote.SSH.remoteServerListenOnSocket.description: When true, the remote vscode server will listen on a socket path instead of opening a port. Only valid for Linux and macOS remotes. Requires `AllowStreamLocalForwarding` to be enabled for the SSH server.

enumDescriptions: Download server on client and upload to server when direct download fails and no jump host is configured
Always prefer downloading server on client and uploading to server
remote.SSH.localServerDownload.markdownDescription:
Controls whether the server should be downloaded on the client and then uploaded to the server. This can help with remote machines that have connectivity issues. Valid values are:
- `auto` - Download locally only when the direct download fails and no jump host is configured
- `always` - Always download locally and upload
- `off` - Never download locally

remote.SSH.forceProxyDownload.markdownDescription:
Always download the server through the proxy instead of letting the target machine download directly. This is useful when:
- Target machine cannot access the download server due to firewall/network restrictions
- Download speed is significantly faster
- You want to ensure consistent proxy usage for security policies

remote.SSH.alwaysUseProxy.markdownDescription:
Always configure proxy for target machine even if it can access public network directly (ping returns pong). When enabled:
- All network requests on target machine (downloads, AI features, extension marketplace, etc.) will use proxy
- Useful when jump host has better network connectivity or bandwidth
- Useful when network policies require all traffic through proxy
- Useful when you want to centralize network access through jump host

Note: This option is only effective when connecting through a jump host with tunnel proxy configured.

remote.SSH.exportProxyEnvToTerminal.markdownDescription:
Controls whether to export proxy environment variables (`ALL_PROXY`, `QODER_JUMP_PROXY`) to terminal sessions when connecting through a jump host.

When enabled (default), the jump host SOCKS proxy URL is injected into all terminal sessions, which allows tools like `curl`, `wget`, and `pip` to route through the proxy automatically.

Disable this if the target machine has direct network access and the injected `ALL_PROXY` causes errors (e.g., `Missing dependencies for SOCKS support` in pip).

Note: This only affects terminal environment variables. The proxy is still used for server installation regardless of this setting.

remote.SSH.experimental.serverBinaryName.description: **Experimental:** The name of the server binary, use this **only if** you are using a client without a corresponding server release
